name: Avon Microtransit
note: Town of Avon is the operator; microtransit replaces certain local routes

name: Basalt Connect
note: Town of Basalt is the operator

name: Call-N-Ride (Greeley-Evans Transit)
note: Service area covers Greeley and Evans

name: County Express
note: Operator NECALG's own site lists County Express dispatchers by county grouping (Morgan; Logan/Phillips/Sedgwick; Washington/Yuma), confirming service across all six counties. https://necalg.org/county-express/

name: Denver Connector
note: Service covers named neighborhoods: Montbello, Gateway, Globeville, Elyria-Swansea, West Denver, Villa Park, Barnum, Westwood, Ruby Hill. Expanded 2024.

name: Downtowner Aspen
note: Service zone is a subset of city limits: bounded by Aspen Mountain to the south, Gillespie and Puppy Smith streets to the north, 8th Street to the west, and Midland/Crystal Lake Road to the east — the downtown core and adjacent neighborhoods, not the full city of Aspen. Source: https://aspen.gov/270/Downtowner

name: Erie Bee
note: Town of Erie service zone. Launched April 21, 2026.

name: Highlands Ranch Microtransit
note: Serves Highlands Ranch with focus on mobility for older adults. Launched spring 2025.

name: Kiowa County Transit
note: Operator is Kiowa County government (Kiowa County Commissioner's Office); service area described as Eads and Haswell, both towns within Kiowa County, with no evidence service is limited to Eads only. Shown as approximate countywide coverage. https://kiowacounty.colorado.gov/government/departments/kiowa-county-transit

name: Larimer Lift
note: Larimer County is the operator and specifies countywide service

name: Link on Demand (Lone Tree)
note: Covers Lone Tree, Highlands Ranch, Stonegate, and Castle Rock (added July 31, 2026) fully; Parker coverage is partial ('select areas of Parker', not the whole town) so the Parker polygon here overstates actual coverage — no boundary streets or map are published outside the operator's in-app service-area tool (City.RideWithVia.com/LinkOnDemand). Meridian also served but ambiguous in boundary data (multiple Meridian CDPs exist); mapped coverage uses other resolved places. Service areas are not continuous. Sources: https://www.douglasco.gov/free-link-on-demand-rideshare-now-available-in-stonegate-and-parts-of-parker/ , https://cityoflonetree.com/link-on-demand/

name: Mountain Village Dial-A-Ride
note: Verified against the operator's own page: Dial-A-Ride is free transportation to "most locations within our town limits" — it does not itself run to Telluride. A separate regional service (SMART, San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation) connects Mountain Village to Telluride; that is a different system, not part of this boundary. Source: https://townofmountainvillage.com/explore/getting-around/bus-dial-a-ride/

name: Ride Free Lafayette
note: Primary service in Lafayette with spillover service to Kestrel community in Louisville.

name: RTD FlexRide
note: RTD's site (rtd-denver.com/routes-services/other-services/flexride) names 16 zones: Brighton, Broomfield, DTC, Evergreen, Federal Heights, Golden, Green Mountain, Interlocken/Westmoor, Longmont, Louisville, Parker, South Jeffco, Superior, Thornton, Wagon Road, plus Broomfield North per the CSV. 10 of these correspond to a real municipality or CDP and are mapped above, but each FlexRide zone covers only part of that place, not the whole city/CDP, so these polygons overstate actual coverage — treat as approximate/oversized. DTC, Green Mountain, Interlocken/Westmoor, South Jeffco, Wagon Road, and Broomfield North have no matching Census place/CDP or county subdivision (checked the Census TIGER CO place file directly — 'Green Mountain' is not a CDP, only 'Green Mountain Falls', a different town near Colorado Springs) and are omitted entirely — those areas are not represented in the boundary at all. Precise zone shapes are only in RTD's interactive map: https://rtd-denver.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/interactivelegend/index.html?appid=b2d921ef0ad040d28c5ce49527793046&locale=en-us

name: Snowmass Village On-Demand Shuttle (Route 22)
note: Winter service is narrower (on-request stops along Wood Rd up to Wood Run V and Faraway Rd up to the Ridge Condominiums), but the summer schedule (June-Sept) expands Route 22 to all accessible, public, paved roads within the Town of Snowmass Village limits, so the town boundary is the correct outer envelope. https://www.villageshuttle.com/217/Route-22On-Demand

name: The Lift Flex
note: Town of Winter Park is the operator

name: Via Mobility - Weld County
note: Not truly countywide: Via's LINK On Call serves a large portion of unincorporated Weld County plus the towns of Fort Lupton, Milliken, Ault, Gilcrest, Hudson, Johnstown, Keenesburg, Kersey, Nunn, and Platteville — it does not cover incorporated Greeley or other larger cities in the county. Weld County polygon used as a containing-unit proxy; actual coverage is smaller/patchier. Operator's own service-area map: bit.ly/WeldCountyMap. Sources: https://viacolorado.org/2023/08/weld-county-announces-new-accessible-transportation-service-for-residents/ , https://coloradocommunitymedia.com/2023/08/09/weld-county-residents-will-have-access-to-transportation-with-via-mobility-services/

name: Yellow Zone
note: City of Steamboat Springs is the operator
